results.title: Top 8 Microsoft Office alternatives for 2026
results.content:
## 4. WPS Office

WPS Office is the alternative that looks and feels like Office. The interface is so familiar you will barely notice you switched, and it is light on system resources, which laptops appreciate.

Standout strengths:

   Near-identical experience to Microsoft Office

   Lightweight and fast

   Strong file compatibility

   Free tier available

Limitations: The free tier serves ads, which can be distracting. Some advanced features sit behind the paid version.

Best for: People who want the Office experience and price relief, and can tolerate a few ads.

## 5. Zoho Workplace [...] ## 3. LibreOffice

LibreOffice is the well-known free, open-source suite: Writer, Calc, Impress, and more, with no subscription, no account, and no catch. It opens and saves Office formats, so it works with the .docx crowd.

Standout strengths:

   Completely free and open source

   Full desktop suite that runs offline

   Solid compatibility with Microsoft formats

   No telemetry, no upsells

Limitations: The interface looks like it is from a decade ago. There is no native cloud collaboration, and complex Office files can occasionally lose a bit of formatting on the round trip.

Best for: Budget-conscious users who want a real, offline office suite and do not mind a dated look.

## 4. WPS Office [...] ### Can these alternatives open my existing Office files?

Most can. LibreOffice, WPS Office, OnlyOffice, and Google Workspace all handle .docx, .xlsx, and .pptx files. Gamma imports PowerPoint, PDF, and Google Slides slide-for-slide at near-perfect fidelity, then lets you restyle them, and it exports back to all three for sharing with Office users.

### Which alternative is best if I mostly make presentations and documents?

Gamma. It is built for exactly that: turning your content into polished decks and docs fast, with AI doing the design work.

### Do I need a full office suite at all?

Often, no. If your work is mostly writing and presenting, a focused tool like Gamma covers the ground you actually use, without the bulk of a full suite.

# What are the best Microsoft Office al­ter­na­tives? 7 solutions compared

 IONOS editorial team7 mins
 + Share on Facebook
  + Share on Twitter
  + Share on LinkedIn
  + Add as a preferred source on Google

Rawpixel.comShut­ter­stock

Free and af­ford­able al­ter­na­tives to Microsoft Office offer many essential office features like word pro­cess­ing, spread­sheets, and pre­sen­ta­tions—often as web or cross-platform apps. Popular choices are well-suited for personal or ed­u­ca­tion­al use but they can also serve as a complete al­ter­na­tive office suite.

## An overview of the Microsoft Office al­ter­na­tives [...] ## Calligra Office

Calligra is available for Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, and Linux, with the suite designed par­tic­u­lar­ly for Linux systems. The full range of programs doesn’t include the al­ter­na­tive to Microsoft Office in all editions. For instance, Windows users only have access to the word pro­cess­ing program (Words) and pre­sen­ta­tion creation (Stage). Apps like the spread­sheet (Sheets) or the project man­age­ment tool (Plan) are reserved for Linux users. The programs are com­pa­ra­ble to those from OpenOf­fice and Li­bre­Of­fice, but they offer sig­nif­i­cant­ly fewer features. Calligra can open Microsoft Office file formats but cannot save them.
